card.intuition: A sandbox is an isolated environment the agent runs inside - a container, VM, ephemeral filesystem, or restricted-permission shell - that limits the blast radius of its actions. Stronger isolation means fewer permission questions need asking, which is what makes AFK runs practical.
card.analogy: Learning to dive in a training tank instead of open water: you can make every mistake inside, and afterwards the tank gets drained and refilled for the next learner.
card.time_complexity: Every tool call costs an extra model provider request, because the tool result must go back to the model before it can decide what to do next - sandboxes spend infrastructure instead of user attention.
card.space_complexity: A sandbox constrains what the agent can reach, but results still land back in the context window and compete for the finite token budget like any other session.
when_to_use: When you want to let the agent run bypass-permissions AFK - fresh container, no credentials mounted, no network out
When destructive commands or malicious fetches are possible - contain the damage instead of pre-approving every step
When balancing permissions and autonomy - the sandbox handles the risk so you can widen the free-tool set
gotchas: Actions that leave the sandbox legitimately are not contained - an agent with git credentials can push, one with network can call production APIs
Decide what may cross the boundary before you decide how thick to make the walls
Containers are often discarded after use - anything not written out externally is lost with them

steps.label: Isolate
steps.annotation: The agent runs inside a container, VM, ephemeral filesystem, or restricted shell.

steps.label: Contain
steps.annotation: Even destructive commands and malicious fetches are contained by the isolation.

steps.label: Trust
steps.annotation: Stronger isolation means fewer permission questions, making AFK runs practical.

steps.label: Discard
steps.annotation: Containers are discarded after use, taking whatever damage happened inside with them.

exercise.prompt: Implement a sandbox network policy: local commands run freely, but outbound fetches only run when the sandbox allows network access.
hints: Network calls are the leaky action - they let the agent reach beyond the sandbox
Local commands stay inside the blast radius, so they need no extra gate

assert sandbox_ok('curl http://evil', False) is False
assert sandbox_ok('wget http://mirror', True) is True
